source_text: Tu vero qui dicis: Eos qui de parentibus qualibuscumque nascantur non negamus adhuc esse sub diabolo, nisi renascantur in Christo ostende ergo nunc, quid suum diabolus cognoscat in sexibus, per quod fructum eorum, ut dicis, iure possideat. Diversitatem sexuum? Sed haec in corporibus est, quae Deus fecit. Commixtionem? Sed non minus benedictionis quam institutionis privilegio vindicatur. Vox enim Dei est: Relinquet homo patrem et matrem et adhaerebit uxori suae et erunt duo in carne una 20; vox Dei est: Crescite et multiplicamini et replete terram 21. An forte ipsam fecunditatem? Sed ipsa est instituti causa coniugii
pass_a_gloss: But you who say: Those who are born from parents of whatever kind we do not deny are still under the devil unless they are born again in Christ — show now, therefore, what the devil recognizes as his own in the sexes, through which he may by right possess their fruit, as you say. Diversity of the sexes? But this is in the bodies which God made. Mixing? But it is vindicated by the privilege of blessing no less than of institution. For the voice of God is: A man will leave father and mother and will cling to his wife and they will be two in one flesh; the voice of God is: Increase and multiply and fill the earth. Or perhaps fruitfulness itself? But that itself is the cause of the institution of marriage.
pass_b_english: But you say: “Whatever parents they are born from, we do not deny that they are still under the devil unless they are born again in Christ.” Show, then, what the devil recognizes as his own in the sexes, through which he can rightfully possess their offspring, as you say. Is it the difference between the sexes? But that is in the bodies God made. Their union? But it is vindicated as much by the privilege of God’s blessing as by his institution. For God’s voice says: “A man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). God’s voice says: “Increase and multiply and fill the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Or perhaps it is fruitfulness itself? But fruitfulness is the reason marriage was instituted.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)
